leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Came to App State directly from the presidency of the University of South Florida (1988-1993), making him an external hire. His decade in Boone included major capital expansion and the founding of the Turchin Center for the Visual Arts. He died in 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor
leaders.priorInstitution: Appalachian State University (same institution; he was App State's chief academic officer for 24 years)
leaders.notes: Officially titled Acting Chancellor for the 2003-04 academic year. He delayed his own retirement in June 2003 to hold the office while the UNC System searched for Borkowski's successor, then retired in 2004 after nearly 40 years at App State. He died May 15, 2026, at age 88.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor
leaders.priorInstitution: Appalachian State University (same institution; he had been dean of its Walker College of Business until 2003)
leaders.notes: A fully internal appointment: he joined the App State accounting faculty in 1983 and was the Walker College of Business's fifth dean before moving into the provost's office. As chancellor he created the College of Health Sciences and moved athletics to the Sun Belt Conference and FBS. He died unexpectedly October 6, 2023, at age 75.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: External hire from Illinois State, where she had been provost since 2008. She was App State's first female chancellor, installed April 2015, and oversaw record enrollment growth past 21,000, roughly $550 million in capital investment, and the launch of the App State Hickory campus. She stepped down effective April 19, 2024, citing significant health challenges; her subsequent role is not publicly documented.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor
leaders.notes: Named interim chancellor by UNC System President Peter Hans on April 19, 2024, the day Everts stepped down. She led the university through Hurricane Helene recovery while interim, which was widely credited in her subsequent permanent selection.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim Chancellor
leaders.notes: Elected by the UNC System Board of Governors on February 27, 2025 after a national search that drew more than 40 applicants, and took office March 1, 2025; formally installed October 3, 2025. She has spent her entire administrative career at App State, joining the finance faculty in 2003 and rising through assistant dean, dean of the Walker College of Business (2016-2020) and provost (2021-2024). No chancellor search is active.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim Dean, School of Medicine
leaders.priorInstitution: Medical College of Georgia (same institution; he joined the MCG faculty in 1978 as chief of gastroenterology)
leaders.nextRole: Retired from the presidency; remained affiliated with the institution as a physician and emeritus faculty member
leaders.notes: Internal promotion; president of the Medical College of Georgia from July 1, 1988 until his retirement February 1, 2001, the longest presidency of the modern era. The institution he led is the direct predecessor of Augusta University. A gastroenterologist, he received the American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy's Rudolf Schindler Award in 1993.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Medical Affairs and Chief Medical Officer, MCG Health Inc.
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences
leaders.notes: Internal promotion, named by the Georgia Board of Regents effective June 1, 2001. A rheumatologist known for Lyme disease research, he left in 2009 to become chancellor of UAMS, where he served until retiring in 2017.

An otolaryngologist and former medical school dean, named interim president of the Medical College of Georgia by the University System of Georgia; he joined MCG October 1, 2009 and held the office until Azziz arrived in 2010. His immediately preceding position could not be verified from an official source.

leaders.priorTitle: Professor and Chair, Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, and Director, Center for Androgen-Related Research and Discovery
leaders.nextRole: Chief Officer for Academic Health and Hospital Affairs
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: State University of New York (SUNY) System Administration
leaders.notes: External hire. He presided over the institution's rebranding to Georgia Health Sciences University (2011) and the contentious consolidation with Augusta State University into Georgia Regents University (2013), and was founding CEO of the Georgia Regents Health System. He announced on January 15, 2015 that he would step down effective June 30, 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Retired; named President Emeritus by the University System of Georgia Board of Regents
leaders.notes: External hire from within the same state system, taking office July 20, 2015; the institution was renamed Augusta University on December 1, 2015, months into his term. He holds undergraduate and graduate degrees from Augusta's legacy institutions. Under him enrollment grew about 25 percent, NIH funding rose 37 percent, and the School of Computer and Cyber Sciences was created. He retired June 30, 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President for Administration and Chief of Staff to the President
leaders.priorInstitution: Augusta University (same institution; he had held that role since July 2015)
leaders.notes: A fully internal appointment named by the Georgia Board of Regents on June 14, 2024 and effective July 1, 2024. An Augusta native and first-generation college graduate, he spent 2001-2015 at Georgia Southern University rising to vice president for external affairs before joining Augusta as Keel's chief of staff. No presidential search is active; the open searches at Augusta are for executive cabinet positions.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Ball State's 11th president and the person in office at the 1996 scope boundary; external hire who came from the presidency of Indiana University of Pennsylvania (1979-1984). His 16-year tenure is among the longest in Ball State history and was honored in the Congressional Record on his 2000 retirement.

Ball State's 12th president. An urban historian, he served as provost and vice president for academic affairs at the University of North Texas from 1990 to 1998, but the position he held immediately before the 2000 Ball State appointment could not be verified from an official source, so it is left blank. He resigned effective January 1, 2004.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Ball State's 13th president, serving roughly seven months as interim after Brownell's resignation. A journalism professor by background, she left the interim role to become president of the University of Indianapolis, where she served until retiring in 2011.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.notes: Ball State's 14th president and its first woman to hold the office permanently; external hire from UMass Boston, where she had been chancellor since 2001 (and before that provost at Old Dominion University). She announced in October 2013 that she would retire June 30, 2014 after a decade marked by large-scale campus construction and the geothermal energy conversion.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Ball State's 15th president, appointed May 2014 and beginning duties August 1, 2014 as an external hire from the University of Maine presidency. A toxicologist, he resigned abruptly on January 25, 2016 after requesting a two-month sabbatical; the board of trustees gave no reason, and his next position is not publicly documented.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Ball State's 16th president, serving as acting president from January 2016 until Mearns took office in 2017. He had also briefly filled the gap between Gora's June 2014 retirement and Ferguson's August 2014 arrival. His post-acting-presidency role is not documented in an official source.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Ball State's 17th president, named January 2017 and taking office in May 2017 as an external hire from Northern Kentucky University, where he had been president since 2012. A former federal prosecutor and law dean at Cleveland State, he oversaw Ball State's 2018 assumption of governance of Muncie Community Schools. Trustees voted May 1, 2026 to extend his contract through June 30, 2029, so no presidential search is active.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: South Dakota School of Mines and Technology
leaders.notes: Boise State's fifth president and the person in office at the 1996 scope boundary; external hire from Virginia Commonwealth University, where he was provost 1985-1993. Under him the operating budget grew from $91.8 million to $222.9 million. After South Dakota Mines (2003-2008) he served interim deanships at Texas Tech and Armstrong State.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Retired; continued hosting the Reader's Corner radio program
leaders.notes: Boise State's sixth president, an external hire and former lieutenant governor of Illinois who had been president of Eastern Kentucky University (1998-2002) before leading the Midwestern Higher Education Compact. His 15-year tenure produced Boise State's 2016 Carnegie doctoral research university designation and major research growth. He announced his retirement in November 2017, effective June 2018.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Returned to the faculty as professor of chemistry and biochemistry; retired in 2025
leaders.notes: Named interim president by the Idaho State Board of Education for the year between Kustra's retirement and Tromp's arrival. He joined the Boise State chemistry department in 1990 and was provost from 2010 to 2018, a period in which the university built Idaho's largest graduate school.

leaders.priorTitle: Campus Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor
leaders.notes: Boise State's seventh president and its first woman president, an external hire who took office July 1, 2019 and was invested October 3, 2019. A Victorian literature scholar and first-generation college graduate, her tenure was politically turbulent, with sustained legislative scrutiny of diversity programming. She announced her departure March 20, 2025 to become the 28th president of the University of Vermont, starting there July 1, 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Student Affairs and Enrollment Management
leaders.notes: Appointed interim president by the Idaho State Board of Education and began May 10, 2025, after spring commencement. He had served at Boise State from 2010 to 2019 and returned as vice president in February 2023. In April 2026 he was named sole finalist and then the 20th president of the University of Montana, starting there July 1, 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Research and Economic Development
leaders.nextRole: Returned to her post as vice president for research and economic development
leaders.notes: Named acting president in May 2026 to cover the short gap between Shinn's departure for Montana and Hahn's July 1, 2026 start; her tenure lasted only weeks. She reported to the State Board in June 2026 that Boise State had met the thresholds for Carnegie R1 research designation.

leaders.priorTitle: Craig M. Berge Dean of the College of Engineering
leaders.notes: Boise State's eighth president, an external hire appointed unanimously by the Idaho State Board of Education on July 1, 2026 after a search conducted under a 2026 Idaho law that closed the process and required naming only a single finalist. A thermal sciences and energy researcher with more than 130 peer-reviewed papers and 12 U.S. patents, he spent 21 years at the University of Florida before Arizona. His appointment was effective July 1, 2026, with on-campus duties required by August 10, 2026, so the 14-month presidential search is now closed.
